title: Shift a block left

blocks.text: `String.indent(n)` with a negative `n` removes indentation. The page lists its edge case: it removes **up to** `|n|` leading whitespace characters per line, never fewer than zero, and like every `indent` call it normalizes line endings and ends the result with `\n`.
Write `Shift.left(String text, int n)` (`n >= 0`). It returns `text` with, on every line, up to `n` leading whitespace characters removed:

items: a line with fewer than `n` leading whitespace characters loses only those, never a character of its text;
a tab is one whitespace character, like a space;

a line may end with `
`, `
` or ``; the result ends every line with `
` only, and **every** line ends with it, the last one included.

cases.says: Each line loses n leading spaces, and every line ends with \n.
A line with fewer than n leading whitespace characters loses only those, never a character of its text.
A tab counts as one leading whitespace character, like a space.
Lines ended by \r\n or \r come out ended by \n.
The result always ends with \n, even when the input does not.

concepts: indent with a negative n removes up to that many leading whitespace characters per line, never more than the line has, and ends every line with \n.
